clue.text: Mind games involving heartless schoolboy and child

indicators.note: the games wrap round the other pieces, as if involving them

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school games

indicators.note: with its heart taken out only the outside letters of schoolboy remain

explanation.surface: A schoolboy and a child are subjected to cruel mind games.
explanation.definitionFit: The psyche is the human soul or spirit, the seat of thought and feeling, so a synonym of mind.

clue.text: Struggle with mobile blocking half of screen icon?

indicators.note: the first half of the word screen is used
the mobile letter blocks the icon by standing inside it

parts.note: an icon is an image
M is short for mobile, as in a mobile phone number

explanation.surface: A phone user struggles with an app that's hiding half the screen icon.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrimmage is a confused scuffle or struggle, and also a passage of play in American football.

clue.text: Bonding of cobalt and hydrogen electron with second charged particle

parts.note: Co is the chemical symbol for cobalt
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen
e is the symbol for an electron
an ion is an electrically charged atom or particle

explanation.surface: A chemistry lesson: cobalt, hydrogen, an electron and an ion bond together.
explanation.definitionFit: Cohesion is the force that holds particles together, i.e. sticking together or bonding.

clue.text: German woman reading English at university

parts.note: the LSE is the London School of Economics, a university college

explanation.surface: A German woman is studying English at a British university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' places E beside the university. The London School of Economics (LSE) is part of the University of London.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common German female first name, so it stands for a German woman.

clue.text: Smart clothes beginning to lend one refinement

indicators.note: the smart word dresses the other letters, wrapping round them

parts.note: smart in the sense of upmarket, elegant

indicators.note: only the opening letter of lend is wanted

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Wearing smart clothes lends a person an air of refinement.
explanation.definitionFit: Polish is elegance or cultivated sophistication of manner, a synonym of refinement.

clue.text: "Cosmic" instruments interpreted Das Lied von der Erde?

parts.note: German for earth, which is a planet
German for song, as an aria is

explanation.surface: Mahler's song cycle Das Lied von der Erde, The Song of the Earth, given a cosmic reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interpreted' asks for a translation: The Song of the Earth becomes the planet's song, PLANET ARIA, with 'von der' (of the) just joining the German words.
explanation.definitionFit: Planetariums are projection devices showing stars and planets on a dome, so instruments of the cosmos.

clue.text: Latitude where returning fish change direction to go north

indicators.note: the fish word comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: an eel is a fish

indicators.note: in a down answer going north means reading upwards, so in reverse

parts.note: to yaw is to swerve or change direction, as a ship or aircraft does

explanation.surface: A navigational note on where migrating fish turn and head north.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is freedom of action or room to manoeuvre, the figurative sense of latitude.

clue.text: Toilet in the middle of street is quite inadequate

indicators.note: the toilet word is placed inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: can is slang for toilet

explanation.surface: A toilet stuck in the middle of the road is hardly adequate provision.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means barely sufficient or less than enough, so quite inadequate.

clue.text: University dons plot against yours truly is inspired

indicators.note: the pieces lean against each other side by side

parts.note: yours truly is the speaker, so I am, contracted

indicators.note: the plot word puts the university letter on, wearing it inside

parts.note: a garden bed is a plot

explanation.surface: University dons are plotting against me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like university teachers but is the verb to put on. In a down answer 'against' simply sets IM next to BUED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being imbued with a quality means being filled or permeated with it, as one is when inspired.

clue.text: Reporter's line backs substance of press release

indicators.note: the spoken word supports the other piece from behind, coming after it
the substance is the inner part, the middle letters
a reporter speaks, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: a queue is a line of waiting people

explanation.surface: A journalist's line supports the gist of a press release.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue someone is to free them from danger or captivity, so to release them.

clue.text: King's present requires money your Royal Highness

parts.note: YR is the written abbreviation of your
RH abbreviates Royal Highness

explanation.surface: A demand addressed to royalty: a king's gift costs money, Your Royal Highness.
explanation.walkthrough: The King is one of the three kings, or Magi, who brought gold, frankincense and the answer to the infant Jesus.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic gum was one of the gifts the Magi, the kings of the Nativity story, presented.

clue.text: Deadlock is stagnation to Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words change places

parts.note: split as stag + nation: a stag is a male deer, so male
the second half, nation, is a country or state

explanation.surface: A deadlock might well be described as stagnation, at least by the Reverend Spooner.
explanation.walkthrough: Stagnation breaks into STAG NATION, i.e. MALE STATE; swapping the opening M and ST gives the answer, which also fits stagnation in its plain sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess this position ends the game with neither side able to win, so figuratively any deadlock or impasse.

clue.text: Limit leading couples to utilising modern steps

indicators.note: the leading couple of letters, the first two, of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A dance instruction: lead couples should keep to modern steps.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun this means the greatest extent possible, the furthest limit, as in 'doing one's very best'.

clue.text: Ant and Dec mostly represented in film as sticklers for detail

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase: behaving as sticklers do

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the film word

parts.note: PIC is short for picture, a film

indicators.note: the letters are presented again in a new order
most of the name is used, all but its last letter

explanation.surface: Ant and Dec, the TV presenting duo, appear in a film as fussy perfectionists.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a British TV presenting double act; 'mostly' drops Dec's C, and 'represented' rearranges the remaining letters into EDANT before they go 'in' the film.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pedantic means fussing over minor rules and precision, which is just how sticklers for detail behave.

clue.text: This can end badly and create disillusionment

indicators.note: the letters are put together badly, out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A warning that this situation will end badly and leave people disappointed.
explanation.definitionFit: To disenchant someone is to free them from illusions, making them disillusioned.

clue.text: Account I throw back in face is Dickensian?

indicators.note: the turned-round letters sit inside the face word

parts.note: the face of a clock or watch is its dial

indicators.note: the run account, I, throw is read backwards

parts.note: to lob is to throw high

explanation.surface: Throwing a bill back in someone's face sounds like a scene from Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives BOLICA, which goes 'in' the face after its third letter. The question mark flags the playful definition: 'what the dickens' is a mild oath, the dickens being the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: The dickens is an old euphemism for the devil, so devilish things are punningly of the dickens.

clue.text: Split's not Croatia's capital for nothing

indicators.note: the following letter is left out

parts.note: clove is a past tense and past participle of cleave, to split

indicators.note: a capital letter here is the initial one of the word

explanation.surface: A geography point: Split is not the capital of Croatia.
explanation.walkthrough: Split is a Croatian port, but here it is the verb: cleave, past tense CLOVE. Removing C (Croatia's capital, signalled by 'not') leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis and other games a score of zero is called love, so it means nothing.

clue.text: Shun East German people taking lives

parts.note: Ost is the German word for east

indicators.note: the people word takes in the other piece

parts.note: a race is a people
lives as in exists, the verb is

explanation.surface: Shunning East German citizens who are taking lives.
explanation.definitionFit: To ostracise is to exclude someone from society, to shun or cold-shoulder them.

clue.text: Alternative to watering can smother briar with weeds reportedly

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece smothers the other by lying on top of it
it is the spoken form of the word that counts

parts.note: to weed is to hoe, so weeds is hoes
a briar is a tobacco pipe made from briar root

explanation.surface: A gardener swaps the watering can for something that drowns the brambles and weeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Briar looks like a thorny shrub but is a smoker's pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A long flexible tube used for watering the garden, an alternative to carrying a can.

clue.text: Run away from line overwhelmed by charge

indicators.note: the line letter is engulfed by the charge, so goes inside it

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

explanation.surface: Someone flees a queue after being swamped by a fine.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to run away from danger, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Sink aboard vessel

parts.note: to flag is to weaken or sink, as energy flags
on as in on board

explanation.surface: A ship goes down with people still aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sink' and 'vessel' suggest a ship, but the vessel is a drinking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large container for wine or ale, a drinking vessel.

clue.text: Rotary machine to help with rice threshing

indicators.note: threshing beats grain about, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A machine is brought in to help with threshing the rice harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: This aircraft is lifted by spinning rotor blades, hence a rotary machine.

clue.text: About to go and come back

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a turn is a go, as in a go at a game

explanation.surface: Someone on the point of leaving and then coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: To return is to go back or come back to a place, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Thinly scattered ashes perhaps evenly distributed

indicators.note: the letters are spread around into a new order
the even letters, second, fourth and so on, are taken

explanation.surface: Cremation ashes perhaps being scattered evenly and thinly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evenly' picks SEPRAS from 'ashes perhaps', and 'distributed' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means meagre and thinly spread out, so thinly scattered.

clue.text: Broadcasts with due deference to Sky nationally?

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
pace, from Latin, is used to mean with all respect to someone one disagrees with

explanation.surface: A broadcaster defers to Sky, the satellite TV company, over national coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky looks like the British satellite broadcaster, a sense the surface plays up, but it is the sky above a country.
explanation.definitionFit: The sky above a nation, over which it claims control, is that country's territorial airspace.

clue.text: 10 perhaps behave like recidivists?

definitions.meaning: the answer to 10 across, a gum from a tree, is an example

explanation.walkthrough: 10 across is MYRRH, an aromatic gum resin; split as RE-SIN the word means to sin again, as repeat offenders do.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrrh is a gum exuded by a tree, so an example; re-sin is to offend once more.

clue.text: Go off record covered by Rush

indicators.note: the record letters sit beneath the rush word, inside it

parts.note: to dart is to rush suddenly
an EP is an extended play record

explanation.surface: A record is released, covered by the rock band Rush.
explanation.walkthrough: Rush is a Canadian rock band in the surface, but the verb in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To go off is to leave or set out, a synonym of depart.

clue.text: Plug terminals of users straight into desktop

indicators.note: terminals here are the ends of each word, their final letters

explanation.surface: Instructions for plugging users' computer terminals straight into a desktop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminals' suggests computer screens, but means the end letters of the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A stop is a plug or stopper that blocks a hole, and to plug a hole is to stop it.

clue.text: Attentive governess perhaps pursues former pupil

indicators.note: the servant comes after the former pupil in the answer

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a school
a governess is an example of a household servant

explanation.surface: A watchful governess chases after one of her former charges.
explanation.definitionFit: An observant person notices things quickly, which is being alert and attentive.

clue.text: Relatively hostile hit man eats mafioso's heart

indicators.note: the hit man swallows the central letter, which goes inside

parts.note: to ice someone is slang for to kill them, so a hit man is one who ices

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A hit man takes a bite out of a gangster's heart, making things even frostier.
explanation.definitionFit: Icy can mean cold and unfriendly, so the comparative form means more hostile than another.

clue.text: Come up with popular way to let off steam?

parts.note: something popular is in, in fashion
a vent is an opening that lets steam escape; also giving vent to feelings

explanation.surface: The fashionable way to vent frustration.
explanation.definitionFit: To invent something is to devise it, or come up with it for the first time.

clue.text: Favour whistleblower according to guards

indicators.note: the outer word stands guard on both sides of the official

parts.note: per means according to, as in per the rules
a ref, or referee, blows a whistle

explanation.surface: Protecting a whistleblower is seen as a favour, by some accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistleblower' suggests someone exposing wrongdoing, but it is the referee with a whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: To favour one option is to like it better than others, a synonym.
